issues.legal_issue: A prior civil decree on a loan does not prevent a debt-relief court from limiting interest under the statutory cap measured on the date of the debt-relief application.
material_facts: The borrower sought relief under the debt-relief statute after a civil court had passed a decree on the mortgage loan.
The original principal remained unpaid when the borrower applied for debt relief.
By the date of the application, the interest claimed under the decree exceeded the principal still due.
issues.conclusion: The debt-relief court had to limit the interest due on the application date to the principal still unpaid on that date, notwithstanding the earlier decree. The Court set aside the lower-court decree and directed entry of a money decree for the principal and capped interest, allowable costs, and pendente lite and future interest at the permitted rate.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 14(4)(a) and 15 of the U. P. Encumbered Estates Act, 1934, a Special Judge must reject a finding in an earlier loan decree to the extent that its effect is inconsistent with the requirement that interest due on the debt-relief application date not exceed the principal then remaining due. The existence of an earlier decree does not alter the relevant date or deprive the applicant of that benefit. Section 14(7), read with section 27, governs the simple money decree and the rate of pendente lite and future interest. The Court disapproved Pandit Ramsagar Prasad v. Mst. Shayama, A.I.R. 1939 Oudh 75, and referred to Rukun-uddin v. Lachhmi Narain, I.L.R. 1945 All. 307, on rejecting decree findings inconsistent with section 14.

rule.if: debt_relief_claim_proceeding and prior_loan_decree and principal_remained_unpaid_at_application and interest_exceeded_unpaid_principal_at_application

predicates.debt_relief_claim_proceeding: A debtor pursued a statutory proceeding in which a judge determines the amount due on a debt.
predicates.prior_loan_decree: A civil court had already passed a decree determining an amount due on the loan before the debt-relief proceeding was considered.
predicates.principal_remained_unpaid_at_application: Some of the loan principal remained unpaid when the debtor applied for debt relief.
predicates.interest_exceeded_unpaid_principal_at_ap: The interest due by the application date exceeded the principal that remained unpaid on that date.

issues.definition: When a debt-relief claim follows an earlier loan decree and unpaid principal remains, interest exceeding that unpaid principal at the application date is limited to that principal.
